name: Mesopotamian Arabic

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Gilit Mesopotamian Arabic (meso1252).

notes: Skeleton. Gelet (gilit) Mesopotamian Arabic, a Semitic (Afroasiatic) variety written in the Arabic abjad. Consonant letters are mapped to IPA; the reflex of qāf ⟨ق⟩ is the voiced velar [ɡ] characteristic of gilit dialects, jīm ⟨ج⟩ is [dʒ], and the interdentals ⟨ث ذ ظ⟩ are retained. Short vowels are not written in the abjad and, apart from the optional harakāt, are left unencoded; gemination (shadda) and stress are likewise not recovered, so a high PER floor is expected. CONFUSABLE AND FORMATTING CODEPOINTS: three Unicode characters that occur in real Arabic-script text had no grapheme entry anywhere in this family, and a character with no entry is dropped without an error, so every occurrence was deleted in silence. ک KEHEH is the Persian/Urdu/Sindhi shape of kaf (annotated '= kaf mashkula') and is read here exactly as ك — [k]. ی FARSI YEH is annotated for Arabic as well as Persian, Urdu and Kashmiri, and is read exactly as ي — [j] or the mater lectionis [iː]. ـ TATWEEL is the kashida, inserted to stretch a word for justification and carrying no sound, so it maps to the empty string: the deletion is now stated instead of accidental, the treatment ٱ ALEF WASLA already had. ہ HEH GOAL is deliberately NOT added — Unicode assigns it to Urdu, and it occurs in none of the Arabic gold. The alternates are listed as bare letters only; a keheh or farsi yeh carrying a harakat does not match the diacritised digraph keys and falls back to the bare letter plus the mark, which yields the same phonemes.

U+06A9 KEHEH is annotated '= kaf mashkula' and assigned to 'Persian, Urdu, Sindhi, ...'; U+06CC FARSI YEH is assigned to 'Arabic, Persian, Urdu, Kashmiri, ...'; U+0640 TATWEEL is '= kashida', 'inserted to stretch characters or to carry tashkil with no base letter'; U+06C1 HEH GOAL is assigned to Urdu only.
